title: Hebron
lead: An old city in the hills of Judah, where Abraham bought a burial cave, Caleb took his inheritance, and David first reigned as king for seven and a half years.

sections.b: Hebron, once called Kiriath-arba (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:15), lies about 19 miles south of Jerusalem. Abraham camped by the oaks of Mamre near it (Genesis 13:18) and bought the cave of Machpelah there to bury Sarah; Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah were buried in it too (Genesis 23; Genesis 49:29–32). The spies saw the sons of Anak there (Numbers 13:22), and Caleb received it (Joshua 14:13–14). It was a city of refuge and a Levite town (Joshua 20:7; Joshua 21:11–13). David reigned there over Judah seven years and six months (2 Samuel 2:1–11; 2 Samuel 5:5), and Absalom began his revolt there (2 Samuel 15:7–10).
